title: Fix IpScriptFieldTypeTests by changing merge policy

timeline.message: Remove merges to ensure term queries test work correctly
timeline.author: carlosdelest

timeline.message: Get better coverage by using random merge policy, without shuffling docs order
timeline.author: carlosdelest

timeline.body:
Random merges in the writer can make this test fail. Use a non-random doc order merge so tests pass.

Similar to https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/104375

Closes #106900

Question - should we expand this fix to the individual term queries [here](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/3deb5ccfe50b413f0d327073f56277ac56642407/server/src/test/java/org/elasticsearch/index/mapper/IpScriptFieldTypeTests.java#L210)? Or are individual term queries not dependent on doc ordering?

reply.body: I think the same applies there too.

timeline.body:
This fix doesn't make sense to me. The result checking doesn't care about document order at all. 

So, I tested this fix running it over a couple thousand of iterations, and it still fails with the same assertion tripping. I am not 100% sure how to fix this test, but it doesn't have to do with the merge policy.

reply.body:
Thanks for checking - I had checked for some hundred iterations and didn't hit a failure.

It's interesting that the change fixed the specific instance though. I'm not sure how to dig deeper into this.

> It's interesting that the change fixed the specific instance though. I'm not sure how to dig deeper into this.

It could be because the random seed generation switched as different values were created. For example (note, my numbers here are fake), in the failing seed, only 4 integers would be created vs. 3 in your version. So, the values that cause the failure wouldn't actually be tripped.

timeline.body: Closing this PR as this doesn't fix the problem - need to think of an alternative approach
